A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Guided Star-Shaped Masked Diffusion. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original OpenWebText experiments, sampling ablations, Conala code-generation results, and Dream-Instruct 7B benchmark evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds temperature-sweep comparisons, cross-domain error-prediction evaluations, and measured inference timings.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same star-shaped sampling, training on model-generated errors, classification objective, and targeted remasking procedure. The hybrid and loop schedules also remain. Expanded head descriptions and methodological explanations do not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds transfer evaluation of the OWT-trained error predictor on TinyStories, OpenWebMath, CNN/DailyMail, and The Stack's Python subset. This introduces explicit out-of-domain error-detection scenarios across stories, mathematics, news, and code. Existing OWT, Conala, Tulu 3, and seven downstream benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds evaluated P2-planner, RDM, and DDPD comparisons beyond v1's MDLM/ReMDM comparisons. Separate ReMDM-conf and cap/rescale rows disappear from the main comparison, although cap/rescale remain in the appendix tuning analysis. The new timing comparison also includes GPT-2 small autoregressive baselines with and without KV caching.

E3.justification: The main OWT comparison introduces denoiser-temperature Pareto sweeps, with 512-step baselines against 128–512-step G-Star. New protocols include 10,000 examples per domain, classification accuracy/AUC-ROC, and batch-one H200 latency measurements. Dream predictor training is reported as Adam at 1e-4 for 10 epochs in v1, versus AdamW at 3e-4 for 70,000 steps in v2; this documentation change does not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds denoiser-temperature quality–diversity analysis, predictor-capacity Pareto comparisons, cross-domain robustness tests, and DDPD/P2 remasking case studies. The earlier activation-time, ReMDM tuning, loop-size, and predictor-temperature analyses remain, as do the original guided/unguided examples.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports latency as mean ± standard deviation. Existing shaded uncertainty bands in generation plots are retained. Neither version specifies seed counts for those plots, and v2 does not state the timing repetition count.

E6.justification: v2 adds temperature-sweep findings, out-of-domain AUC-ROC scores of 0.90–0.98, and timing results such as 3.43 ± 0.10 seconds for 128-step G-Star-loop12B,H. Many detailed OWT point results from v1 Table 1 disappear. Conala and all seven Dream benchmark scores remain identical; the new results do not demonstrate same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Proposition 1 and a proof of the previously asserted ReMDM equivalence; the VLB proof remains unchanged. Appendix D adds an NFE derivation. Local mathematical regressions accompany these additions: Equation (17) changes the mask coefficient so probabilities generally fail to normalize, and the defined guided-step fraction has the opposite sign to its numerical use.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims: pretrained-compatible G-Star uses lightweight learned error correction to improve few-step text/code generation and enhance a 7B model. The expanded contribution list principally restates compatibility, late-stage refinement, and frozen-head findings already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving confidence calibration, synthetic-noise mismatch, and why conditioning refinement on the current state can impede correction. It revises the favorable interpretation of the one-block predictor and quantifies approximately 50% full-depth latency overhead. Cross-domain transfer interpretations and a limitation concerning unoptimized inference are added; the earlier insertion/deletion and separate-training limitations remain.

D1.justification: New disclosures include the OWT predictor's 50,000-step training recipe, hardware and training times, Dream's RMSNorm-plus-linear head and optimizer schedule, and detailed compute/memory accounting. Appendix G adds practical schedule and temperature guidance. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the supplementary-code availability statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 and Appendix B substantially expand positioning against confidence-based sampling, stochastic remasking, and trained refiners. v2 discusses concurrent Kim and Huang studies and explicitly distinguishes its pretrained-compatible formulation from Okhotin's original star-shaped framework. Additional references support the new transfer datasets and inference-acceleration discussion.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, and Sections 4.4–4.5 are extensively rewritten. Appendices are reorganized around theory, computational overhead, implementation, examples, and practical guidance; the earlier standalone refinement example is incorporated into Appendix F. Terminology, author listing, publication header, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: The main OWT score table is replaced by two Pareto panels. v2 adds robustness and timing tables, a schedule diagram, and DDPD/P2 trajectory plots. Existing figures are resized or relocated, the conceptual sampler diagram gains annotations, and the unchanged Dream and Conala tables exchange positions.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator set and temperature-swept evaluation substantially strengthen v1's limited empirical comparison. Cross-domain tests, measured runtime costs, and previously missing OWT training details make effectiveness, transfer, and efficiency more assessable. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed OWT point results and the localized formula inconsistencies in Appendices A.2 and D, although those inconsistencies still require correction.
